vercel.note: REAL INCIDENT this capture: AUTH_RESEND_KEY had an empty string value on BOTH Production and Preview (set ~26 days ago, never actually given a value, or a value that got lost — root cause not determined). Result: every Resend email send in the app had been silently no-op'ing for an unknown period, since `if (key) {...}` is false on an empty string. Found while testing the new lead-alert feature, fixed by Zach re-saving it as a Sensitive var (confirmed live via real test send — arrived). No code change required; this was purely an env-var data problem. Worth a periodic real-send check on email features going forward, since failures here are silent by design (delivery failures must not break the calling request).

serialization_protocol.design: per-branch state files — each branch owns _STATE/branch-<slug>.json and never overwrites the shared snapshot/session-state; main reconciles on merge.
serialization_protocol.arcs_v9_stance: ADOPT the per-branch-file convention for /handoff on feature branches; do NOT host the lock-manager implementation.
serialization_protocol.compliance_note: NOT FOLLOWED this week — no _STATE/branch-claude-sleepy-booth-889373.json was ever created, and the merge-time reconciliation into this file didn't happen until this capture, 6 days and 3 follow-on commits late. The protocol is still right; the discipline of actually doing it on every branch/merge is the gap. If you're an agent picking this up: create the per-branch file BEFORE your first commit on a new branch, not as an afterthought.
